bashCommands.modeAuthoritative: Authoritative mode: these lists are the complete policy for bash commands. Anything not explicitly trusted will prompt for approval.
bashCommands.modeInactive: Not configured. The default bash rule applies to all commands. Add at least one trusted pattern or denylist entry to enable fine-grained control.
bashCommands.trustedDesc: One pattern per line. Prefix-matched; use `*` as a wildcard. Matching commands run without a prompt. Each sub-command in a chain (&&, ||, ;, |) is checked independently.
bashCommands.denylistDesc: One pattern per line. Substring-matched. Any command containing a denylist entry always prompts, even if it also matches the trusted list.
bashCommands.trustedDirectoriesDesc: One directory per line. A write inside these directories runs without a prompt; a write anywhere else asks. Applies to the write and edit tools and to the places a bash command visibly writes (output redirections, tee). `./` means the session's workspace. Leave empty to turn the check off.
bashCommands.trustedDirectoriesNote: This checks visible writes — it is not a sandbox: what a program writes on its own cannot be seen. The file-system root and the home directory are not accepted as entries. A bash command must still pass the lists above.
bashCommands.safetyNote: Shell syntax that cannot be read safely (command substitution, process substitution, subshells, lone background &) always prompts, even when a matching trusted pattern exists. A line break separates commands like `;` — each one is checked on its own.

memory.advancedHelpIntro: When you ask the assistant about something from a past conversation, it searches your chat history and ranks results by relevance.
memory.advancedHelpFormula: The scoring formula: score = relevance + recency boost − supersession penalty
memory.advancedHelpRecencyDesc: Newer conversations get a small advantage over older ones. This helps when facts change over time (e.g., you updated your app version).
memory.advancedHelpRecencyCeiling: Recency ceiling — how much boost a brand-new conversation gets. Higher means newer info wins more easily.
memory.advancedHelpRecencyFloor: Recency floor — minimum boost even for very old conversations. Higher means old info stays more relevant.
memory.advancedHelpRecencyDecay: Decay period — how many days until the boost drops from ceiling to floor.
memory.advancedHelpSupersessionDesc: When a newer conversation covers the same topic as an older one, the older one gets penalized. This prevents outdated info from winning by volume (e.g., 50 old chats saying "v2.17" vs 1 new chat saying "v2.25").
memory.advancedHelpSupersessionPenalty: Supersession penalty — how much to penalize the older conversation. Higher means newer wins more.
memory.advancedHelpSupersessionThreshold: Keyword threshold — how similar topics must be to trigger the penalty. Higher means stricter matching (fewer false positives).
memory.advancedHelpPromptDesc: After each conversation, a background process decides what to remember about you (preferences, skills, identity). The extraction prompt controls how selective this process is. The built-in default is tuned for most users. Custom prompts let you change what gets remembered and what gets ignored.
memory.recencyDecayDaysHint: Days until boost drops from ceiling to floor (30–180)
memory.supersessionPenaltyHint: Score penalty for older same-topic chunks (0–0.5)
